text:
alex: quick q — who's allowed to approve a PR that changes CODEOWNERS entries for /shared/libs/runtime? I'm about to merge a tiny rename but it's touching owners file. cc @sam @tara :thinking:

sam: if it's only renames and path tweaks, infra-owners can approve. But the current CODEOWNERS line is something like ` /shared/libs/runtime/ @eng-runtime ` — can you paste the PR link? :eyes:

alex: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-platform/pull/8423

alex: diff:
```
- /shared/libs/runtime/ @eng-runtime
+ /shared/libs/runtime/v2/ @eng-runtime @eng-platform
```

tara: hmm adding @eng-platform is a scope change (it broadens who owns those files). We usually require at least one approver from each listed team. I can approve if joel or another eng-platform maintainer gives a quick +1.

joel: I can take a look in ~20m. If it's purely a path rename (no packaging/deploy surface) it's fine. If it touches build / package.json or the deploy scripts we need both eng-runtime + eng-platform approvals. :white_check_mark:

deploy-bot: CI: build passed ✅, unit tests passed, integration tests queued.

sam: to be safe, update the PR description explaining why eng-platform is being added, and ping the eng-platform lead in the thread so we have explicit cross-team signoff.

alex: good call — I'll update the PR and tag joel. holding merge until I get +2 (eng-runtime + eng-platform) or explicit owner from eng-platform.

joel: reviewed now — no packaging or scripts touched. Code change is just a rename and CODEOWNERS update. +1 from me.

tara: +1 from me too, feel free to merge once CI finishes. :shipit:

alex: merging in 5m, thanks everyone :tada:
